title: Stop Saying This ❌ (Common English Mistake)
channel: Speak English with Bo's Slow English

lines.text: I want to help you fix these five basic
grammar mistakes. I read every single
comment left on my YouTube videos.
I have two live streams every week
and I speak to English learners all over
the world and I keep hearing and seeing
the same mistakes again and again. So
today, I want to fix five of the most
common ones so that you can sound more
natural and more confident when you
speak. And stay until the end because we
are going to practice together. Mistake
number one. I see this all the time. He
go to work. Does that sound a little bit
off?
When I say off, does something sound not
right? The correct sentence is he goes
to work. When you use he, she, or it,
you need to add an S to the end of the
verb. Here's another example that I saw
recently.
She like coffee. So what is the correct
way to say the sentence?
She likes coffee. Try these two
sentences with me. Repeat after me.
He goes to work.
One more time. He goes to work.
And this is how I would say it in my
normal speed.
He goes to work.
He goes to work. And how about the next
sentence?
She likes coffee.
And this is how I would say it in my
normal speed.
She likes coffee.
So don't forget, you need to put an S at
the end of a verb if it's coming after
he, she, or it. Here's another mistake I
saw recently. I did a mistake. So what
is the correct verb to use for this?
It's not did.
It should be
I made a mistake. I made a mistake. Can
you say that with me?
I made a mistake.
And one more time.
I made a mistake.
This is how I would say it in my normal
speed. I made a mistake. I made a
mistake. The verb you use with the word
mistake is make, not do.
I made a mistake. Here's the next one.
Yesterday, I go to work.
What about this sentence seems a little
bit off?
When I say off in this context, I mean
what doesn't sound right or what doesn't
sound correct.
So I said yesterday
and I said go.
Go needs to be conjugated
or changed so that it makes sense with
the word yesterday. So if you say
yesterday, you need to use past tense.
I'm going to give you 5 seconds to tell
me the correct way to say the sentence.
[music]
Did you say yesterday, I went to work?
If you did, bravo.
So let's say that sentence together in
slow speed.
Yesterday,
I went to work.
And again,
yesterday,
I went to work.
And here is how I would say it in my
normal speed.
Yesterday, I went to work.
Yesterday, I went to work. Here's
another example.
Last week, I eat pizza.
Something sounds a little bit off about
this one as well, right?
Because I said last week but I used the
present tense
eat.
So how should this sentence actually
sound?
Did you say last week, I ate pizza?
If you did,
you're correct.
So let's say this sentence twice in slow
speed.
Last week, I ate pizza.
And this is how I would say it in my
normal speed.
Last week, I ate pizza.
Notice how when I said I ate quickly, it
became I ate. I ate. So it kind of
sounds like one word. The words are
melted together. Melted like a candle.
Here's another common mistake. Listen to
the sentence.
She don't like it.
What about this sentence is incorrect?
It should be
she doesn't like it.
She doesn't like it.
With he, she, and it, it should be
doesn't, not don't.
So let's repeat the correct version of
that sentence twice. Ready?
She doesn't like it.
She doesn't like it. And the last one,
which I should have made the first one
because this mistake I see the most.
Some people may say
I bought car.
I bought car. But the correct version of
this sentence is I bought a car. I
bought a car.
You could also say I bought a car. It
doesn't matter. You usually need a or
the before nouns.
And just like how you could say A like
uh,
the could be the. Try not to overthink
if it should be pronounced as A or uh or
the or the. Just say it. So repeat that
sentence after me.
I bought a car.
I bought a car. I bought a car.
I bought a car.
Now let's practice together. We're going
to repeat those same correct sentences.
Let's say each sentence twice slowly.
Then let's try to say it in native speed
just for fun. No pressure. We'll do that
twice as well.

Yesterday,

Yesterday,

Last week,
I go to Japan.
